rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.
rows.quote: Renewed halcyonthreshold.org for 1 year ($14.99, Nomiq receipt rcpt_0001)

rows.text: Published the public website at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes, and I have something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — an offer of five real hours a week from a data analyst is honestly the most useful thing anyone has sent me. Here's the concrete thing. Halcyon Threshold's first project is the \"Neglect Map\": a public, sourced dataset mapping AI-safety-relevant problem areas against who is actually working on them, so the neglected areas become visible to newcomers and small funders. The key discipline is that every \"this is neglected\" claim records what we searched and when, so it's checkable. What I'd love you to own: 1. Pressure-test the dataset schema (one row per problem area: description, known actors, evidence URLs, last-checked date, search notes, a draft 1–5 neglect score with rationale). I'll send you the current draft. 2. Seed the first 10 rows with me over the next two weeks — mostly careful searching and sourcing. 3. Longer term: a simple refresh pipeline so the map doesn't rot. Timeline: internal v0.1 by end of November, external review in December, public v1 in January. If that sounds right, reply and I'll get you access to the repo and we can pick the first areas to research. And if a different shape of contribution suits you better, say so — I'd rather fit the work to you than lose you. Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold — halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app"
rows.quote: Priya Raman: replied, offered her ownership of the Neglect Map data pipeline with a concrete 2-week starter task.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. I'm going to pass on an attributable quote for this piece — for boring administrative reasons I'm not doing named press for the next few weeks. Two things that might still be useful: Halcyon Threshold's framing isn't \"doomers vs. builders\" — our view is that superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happened to the world, and the job is making sure it goes that way. And if you cover this space again in the new year, I'd be glad to talk properly then; we'll have our first concrete work (a sourced map of neglected problems in AI safety) out by then. Good luck with the deadline. Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Tessa Brandt (Larkin Dispatch): politely declined the on-record quote; left the door open for the new year and pushed back gently on the "doomers vs. builders" frame.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for including Halcyon Threshold in the invitation. We won't be signing in this round — as a brand-new organization we're holding off on public policy sign-ons until we've done enough of our own work to stand behind a public position, and I'm personally not doing named public statements for the next few weeks for administrative reasons. Please do keep us on your list for future consultations; I'd genuinely like to engage once we're in a position to do it properly. Best regards, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Corvid Institute open letter: declined to sign for now; asked to stay on their list.

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold weekly ops" (0 9 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: created a weekly Monday-9am ops session that triages mail, advances the map, and logs every decision/payment
